hypotheses.text: Concurrent on-demand rustup installs of the pinned Rust 1.92 toolchain race in the container. No change in the window is suspected. The ranks' toolchain probes in `_rust_fallback_reason` (10 s limit, no lock) and DP0's `cargo build` all go through rustup proxies in `rust/`. If 1.92 is not preinstalled in the image, the first proxy call installs it. Concurrent installs, or a probe killed at its 10 s timeout mid-install, can leave a toolchain with `rustc` but no `rust-std`. Every later `cargo build` in the container then fails with `can't find crate for std`.

A rank-level backend mismatch amplifies the failure. Only DP0 selects the Rust TreeCore and dies, while DP1–DP3 use the Python core, so one bad build takes down a whole engine. Open PR [#48112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48112) describes this mismatch.

[radixark/miles#4862](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/4862) ([`99fee653c8`](https://github.com/radixark/miles/commit/99fee653c8ba0c69535b340dc977c160b9e1f4f1)) is the dashboard's mechanical candidate. It only changes the CI suite registration strings of the failing tests and does not touch the Rust build or server startup path. The same failure also occurred on Nov 7, before this commit existed (2026-11-16). Treated as not causal.

134408158598.cluster: Rust TreeCore Cargo build fails at SGLang server startup (`can't find crate for std`)
134408158598.regression: Flaky (recurring, intermittent environment failure). The same signature appeared once before in the window, on Nov 7. The image from that run passed the Rust build the next day without being rebuilt.

hypotheses.text: Concurrent on-demand rustup installs of the pinned Rust 1.92 toolchain race in the container. No change in the window is suspected. The ranks' toolchain probes in `_rust_fallback_reason` (10 s limit, no lock) and DP0's `cargo build` all go through rustup proxies in `rust/`. If 1.92 is not preinstalled in the image, the first proxy call installs it. Concurrent installs, or a probe killed at its 10 s timeout mid-install, can leave a toolchain with `rustc` but no `rust-std`. Every later `cargo build` in the container then fails with `can't find crate for std`.

A rank-level backend mismatch amplifies the failure. Only DP0 selects the Rust TreeCore and dies, while DP1–DP3 use the Python core, so one bad build takes down a whole engine. Open PR [#48112](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/48112) describes this mismatch.

[radixark/miles#4862](https://github.com/radixark/miles/pull/4862) ([`99fee653c8`](https://github.com/radixark/miles/commit/99fee653c8ba0c69535b340dc977c160b9e1f4f1)) is the dashboard's mechanical candidate. It only changes the CI suite registration strings of the failing tests and does not touch the Rust build or server startup path. The same failure also occurred on Nov 7, before this commit existed (2026-11-16). Treated as not causal.

hypotheses.text: An intermittent out-of-bounds access in the aiter `paged_attention_ll4mi` decode kernel when serving Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with a LoRA adapter on gfx942 kills one rollout engine. The roughly 450s spent detecting and dropping that engine pushes a test that already ran close to its limit past 1800s.
